summary: TTM Squeeze: momentum histogram with dots that show when Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels.
overview: The TTM Squeeze, by John Carter, shows two things in its own pane. A histogram shows momentum, and dots on the zero line show whether the market is in a squeeze.
Orange dots mean the squeeze is on; gray dots mean it is off. A cross on the zero line marks the first bar after a squeeze ends (a fire).
how: Squeeze is on when both Bollinger Bands (20 bars, 2 deviations) are inside the Keltner Channels (20 bars, 1.5 ATR).
Momentum is a linear regression of price minus the average of the Donchian midline and the SMA over 20 bars. Bars are solid when building away from zero and dim when fading back.
use: Some traders watch for the first gray dot after a run of orange dots.
Use the histogram color to see momentum direction at the fire.
Watch for momentum fading as a sign a move is slowing.
Use a long squeeze as a sign of building pressure.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
